arguments.value: Cremer agreed to supply Ultragenyx with triheptanoin in bulk, and Ultragenyx agreed to buy it exclusively from Cremer for a defined field of use. Cremer must provide product that meets specified quality standards, GMP requirements, and supporting documents, and Ultragenyx will place orders by purchase order and make payment in euros after invoicing. The product is delivered EXW unless otherwise agreed, and title passes only after full payment. Pricing is set for each contract year with limits on how much it can rise, and if the parties cannot agree on a new price, Cremer may stop deliveries. Ultragenyx is responsible for final product release and may reject nonconforming product, in which case Cremer must replace it or refund the price. Cremer does not guarantee the product’s pharmaceutical effectiveness, safety, or suitability for Ultragenyx’s intended use, and its liability is largely limited to intentional misconduct or gross negligence. Each party must indemnify the other for third-party claims arising from its own wrongdoing. The agreement lasts three years and renews automatically for two-year periods unless either side gives notice not to renew; it can also be terminated for uncured material breach. German law governs the agreement, disputes must be brought in Hamburg, and the document includes standard clauses on confidentiality, amendments, notices, and development work that may be handled under separate statements of work.
